results.title: Locally nilpotent subgroup
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A subgroup $N$ of a group $G$ is locally nilpotent when every subgroup generated by finitely many elements of $N$ is nilpotent.

results.title: Hirsch–Plotkin radical
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Hirsch–Plotkin radical of a group $G$ is the subgroup generated by all locally nilpotent normal subgroups of $G$. By the Hirsch–Plotkin theorem it is the largest locally nilpotent normal subgroup of $G$.

results.title: Locally nilpotent group (Kourovka 13.16)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A group $G$ is locally nilpotent if for every finite subset $S \subseteq G$ the subgroup generated by $S$ is nilpotent, that is, every finitely generated subgroup of $G$ is nilpotent.

results.title: Minimal condition on centralizers (Kourovka 13.16)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a subset $X$ of a group $G$, let $C_G(X)$ be its centralizer, the subgroup of elements of $G$ that commute with every element of $X$. The group $G$ satisfies the minimal condition on centralizers if every nonempty set of such centralizers has a minimal element with respect to inclusion; equivalently, there is no infinite strictly descending chain $C_G(X_0) > C_G(X_1) > \cdots$ of centralizers.

results.title: Hypercentral group (Kourovka 13.16)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A group $G$ is hypercentral if for every proper normal subgroup $N$ of $G$ there is some $g \in G$ with $g \notin N$ and $g h g^{-1} h^{-1} \in N$ for all $h \in G$; that is, every nontrivial quotient $G/N$ has nontrivial centre (equivalently, the transfinite upper central series of $G$ reaches $G$).

results.title: Kourovka Problem 13.16 (Wagner)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The proposition that every locally nilpotent group satisfying the minimal condition on centralizers is hypercentral.

results.title: Locally nilpotent groups with the minimal condition on centralizers are hypercentral
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every locally nilpotent group satisfying the minimal condition on centralizers is hypercentral. This answers Kourovka Problem 13.16 (F. O. Wagner) in the affirmative (V. V. Bludov, 1998).

results.title: The sequence $A_p$

results.summary: For a natural number $p \ge 1$, $A_p : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$ is the unique sequence with $A_p(n) = 0$ for $-p \le n \le 0$ and $A_p(n) = 1$ for $1 \le n \le p$ that satisfies $A_p(n) = A_p(n-1) + A_p(n-p) - A_p(n-2p-1)$ for every integer $n$. results.title: The two-sided sequence $B_p$

results.title: The companion matrix $Q_p$

results.title: Entry formula for the powers of $Q_p$

results.title: Lucas-type recurrence lists
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type with a zero, a one and an addition, let $p$ be a natural number and let $a_0, c \in \alpha$. results.title: Multiply recurrent point
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $X$ be a topological space and $T \colon X \to X$ a map. A point $x \in X$ is multiply recurrent for $T$ if for every integer $d \ge 1$ there is a strictly increasing sequence of natural numbers $(n_k)$ such that $T^{j n_k}(x) \to x$ as $k \to \infty$ for every integer $j$ with $1 \le j \le d$, where $T^{m}$ denotes the $m$-th iterate of $T$.

results.title: Interlacing of consecutive minuscule polynomials
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n \ge 2$. There are nonzero real numbers $c, d$ and real numbers $r_0 \le \dots \le r_{n-1}$ and $s_0 \le \dots \le s_{n-2}$ such that the type-A minuscule polynomials factor over $\mathbb{R}$ as $N_{n+1}(x) = c \prod_{i=0}^{n-1} (x - r_i)$ and $N_n(x) = d \prod_{j=0}^{n-2} (x - s_j)$, and $r_j \le s_j \le r_{j+1}$ for every $j$ with $0 \le j \le n - 2$.

results.title: Gamma-positivity of the minuscule polynomials

results.title: Exponential generating function of the minuscule polynomials

results.title: Heap assertion
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: A heap assertion is a predicate on a store and a heap: it assigns a proposition to every store $s$ and every heap $h$. Heap assertions serve as the preconditions and postconditions of separation logic.

results.title: Entailment of heap assertions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A heap assertion $P$ entails a heap assertion $Q$ when, for every store $s$ and every heap $h$, if $P$ holds of $s$ and $h$, then $Q$ holds of $s$ and $h$.

results.title: Empty-heap assertion
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The heap assertion $\mathrm{emp}$ holds of a store $s$ and a heap $h$ exactly when $h$ is the empty heap, whatever the store $s$ is.

results.title: Pure assertion
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a proposition $p$, the pure assertion of $p$ holds of a store $s$ and a heap $h$ exactly when $h$ is the empty heap and $p$ is true.

results.title: Points-to assertion
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $a$ and $v$, the assertion $a \mapsto v$ holds of a store $s$ and a heap $h$ exactly when $h$ is the singleton heap that maps the address $a$ to the value $v$ and allocates no other address.

results.title: Separating conjunction
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For heap assertions $P$ and $Q$, the assertion $P \star Q$ holds of a store $s$ and a heap $h$ when there are disjoint heaps $h_1$ and $h_2$ with $h = h_1 \cup h_2$ such that $P(s, h_1)$ and $Q(s, h_2)$.

results.title: Existential heap assertion
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a function $p$ assigning a heap assertion $p(n)$ to each natural number $n$ (an address or a value), the assertion $\exists n,\ p(n)$ holds of a store $s$ and a heap $h$ exactly when $p(n)$ holds of $s$ and $h$ for some natural number $n$.

results.title: Conjunction of heap assertions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For heap assertions $P$ and $Q$, the assertion $P \wedge Q$ holds of a store $s$ and a heap $h$ exactly when $P$ holds of $s$ and $h$ and $Q$ holds of $s$ and the same heap $h$.

results.title: Linear moment model for instrumental variables
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: An observational linear moment model: variables `Z`, `X`, `Y` and `U` on a probability space, all square integrable, with the algebraic decomposition `Y = α + β X + U`. The residual `U` is an arbitrary observed-variable function. Consequently `outcome_eq` does not exclude direct effects of `Z` under interventions, and `β` is only the coefficient in this decomposition. Orthogonality (`Cov(Z, U) = 0`) and nonzero…

results.title: Covariance with the outcome in a linear moment model
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The covariance of any square-integrable variable with the outcome splits along the observational decomposition: `Cov(V, Y) = β Cov(V, X) + Cov(V, U)`.

results.title: Wald ratio identity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The Wald covariance identity: if `Cov(Z, U) = 0` and `Cov(Z, X) ≠ 0`, then `Cov(Z, Y) / Cov(Z, X) = β`. For a two-valued `Z` the ratio is the grouping estimator of Wald (1940), the difference of the group means of `Y` over that of `X`. This is a moment-condition identity, not a formal causal-identification result.

results.title: Wald ratio identity for an instrument independent of the residual
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The Wald covariance identity when the instrument is independent of the residual.

results.title: Wald ratio as a ratio of regression slopes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The Wald ratio as a ratio of regression slopes: the slope of `Y` on `Z` divided by the slope of `X` on `Z` (the form used with SNP–outcome and SNP–exposure associations) is `β`. This is again an observational moment identity.

results.title: Bias of the ordinary least-squares coefficient under confounding
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The ordinary least-squares coefficient identity for `Y` on `X` is `β + Cov(X, U) / Var(X)`, which differs from `β` exactly when `Cov(X, U) ≠ 0`.

results.title: Ratio estimate of a single SNP
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The ratio estimate `β̂_{Yj} / β̂_{Xj}` of SNP `j` (Lean's `x / 0 = 0` gives `0` when `β̂_{Xj} = 0`; such SNPs carry weight `0` in `ivwWeight`).

results.title: Inverse-variance weight of a ratio estimate
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The first-order inverse-variance weight `w_j = β̂_{Xj}² / σ_j²` of the ratio estimate of SNP `j`, where `σ_j` is the standard error of `β̂_{Yj}` (Burgess, Butterworth & Thompson 2013).

results.title: Inverse-variance-weighted estimator
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The inverse-variance-weighted (IVW) estimator `∑ β̂_{Xj} β̂_{Yj} σ_j⁻² / ∑ β̂_{Xj}² σ_j⁻²` (Burgess, Butterworth & Thompson 2013). The standard errors are positive in the model; it is the junk value `0` if every `β̂_{Xj} = 0`.

results.title: Weighted residual sum of squares through the origin
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The weighted residual sum of squares `∑ (β̂_{Yj} - b β̂_{Xj})² / σ_j²` of the regression through the origin with slope `b`.

results.title: IVW estimator as a weighted mean of ratio estimates
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The IVW estimator is the weighted mean of the ratio estimates with weights `w_j = β̂_{Xj}² / σ_j²`. This holds for all data: a SNP with `β̂_{Xj} = 0` has weight `0` and contributes nothing to either side.

results.title: IVW estimator minimizes the weighted residual sum of squares
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The IVW estimator is the weighted least-squares slope through the origin: it minimizes the weighted residual sum of squares. This holds for all data: if every `β̂_{Xj} = 0` the sum does not depend on the slope (and `ivw` is the junk value `0`), and a SNP with `σ_j = 0` has weight `0` on both sides by Lean's `x / 0 = 0`.

results.title: Positivity of the total IVW weight
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The total weight is positive as soon as some SNP has `β̂_{Xj} ≠ 0`.

results.title: IVW recovers an exact proportionality coefficient
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Without error, IVW recovers the proportionality coefficient: if `β̂_{Yj} = β β̂_{Xj}` for all `j` and some `β̂_{Xj} ≠ 0`, then the IVW estimate is `β`. This algebraic statement does not itself give `β` a causal interpretation.

results.title: Unbiasedness of the IVW estimator
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Unbiasedness of IVW (Burgess, Butterworth & Thompson 2013), with the SNP–exposure associations `β̂_{Xj}` treated as fixed: if `β̂_{Yj} = β β̂_{Xj} + ε_j` with integrable mean-zero errors, the IVW estimator has mean `β`.

results.title: Variance of the IVW estimator
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The first-order variance of IVW (Burgess, Butterworth & Thompson 2013): with the `β̂_{Xj}` fixed and `β̂_{Yj} = β β̂_{Xj} + ε_j`, where the errors are square integrable, pairwise uncorrelated (for instance independent) and `Var(ε_j) = σ_j²`, the IVW estimator has variance `(∑ w_j)⁻¹ = (∑ β̂_{Xj}² / σ_j²)⁻¹`.

results.title: Weighted mean
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The weighted mean `∑ v_j a_j / ∑ v_j`.

results.title: Weighted covariance
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The weighted covariance `∑ v_j (a_j - ā_v)(b_j - b̄_v) / ∑ v_j`, where `ā_v` and `b̄_v` are weighted means.

results.title: MR-Egger slope
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The MR-Egger slope (Bowden, Davey Smith & Burgess 2015): the slope of the weighted linear regression of `β̂_{Yj}` on `β̂_{Xj}` with an intercept, `Cov_v(β̂_X, β̂_Y) / Var_v(β̂_X)`. The paper's weights are `v_j = σ_j⁻²`.

results.title: MR-Egger intercept
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The MR-Egger intercept `β̂̄_Y - slope · β̂̄_X` (weighted means).

results.title: Weighted residual sum of squares of a line
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The weighted residual sum of squares `∑ v_j (β̂_{Yj} - a - b β̂_{Xj})²` of the line with intercept `a` and slope `b`.

results.title: MR-Egger line is the weighted least-squares line
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The MR-Egger line is the weighted least-squares line: for nonnegative weights and `β̂_X` of nonzero weighted variance (so the total weight is positive and `β̂_X` is not constant on the support of the weights), it minimizes the weighted residual sum of squares.

results.title: MR-Egger slope under pleiotropy
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The MR-Egger slope under pleiotropy (Bowden, Davey Smith & Burgess 2015): if the SNP–outcome associations are `Γ_j = α_j + β γ_j`, with pleiotropic terms `α_j` and SNP–exposure associations `γ_j`, the Egger slope of `Γ` on `γ` is `β + Cov_v(γ, α) / Var_v(γ)`.

results.title: MR-Egger intercept under pleiotropy
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The MR-Egger intercept under pleiotropy: it is the weighted mean pleiotropic effect `ᾱ_v` minus `Cov_v(γ, α) / Var_v(γ) · γ̄_v`.

results.title: InSIDE identity for MR-Egger
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The finite-sample InSIDE identity (Bowden, Davey Smith & Burgess 2015): if the pleiotropic terms are uncorrelated with the instrument strengths in the weighted sense, `Cov_v(α, γ) = 0`, the MR-Egger slope is the coefficient `β` and the intercept is the weighted mean pleiotropic term `ᾱ_v`. This identity alone does not encode a causal interpretation.

results.title: Directional pleiotropy biases the IVW estimator
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Directional pleiotropy biases IVW: if `Γ_j = α_j + β γ_j`, the IVW estimate is `β + ∑ γ_j α_j σ_j⁻² / ∑ γ_j² σ_j⁻²`. For example a common pleiotropic term `α_j = α ≠ 0` biases IVW whenever `∑ γ_j σ_j⁻² ≠ 0`, whereas a constant `α` satisfies InSIDE, so `eggerSlope_eq_of_inside` gives MR-Egger slope `β` and intercept `α`.

results.title: Ratio with a Gaussian denominator has infinite first moment
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A ratio with a Gaussian denominator has no first moment (a classical fact, recalled in the weak-instrument analysis of Burgess & Thompson 2011): if `D ~ N(m, v)` with `v > 0` and `N` is independent of `D` and not almost surely `0`, then `𝔼|N / D| = ∞`. Applied to the ratio estimator `β̂_Y / β̂_X` with a normally distributed SNP–exposure estimate `β̂_X`.

results.title: Ratio of independent normal variables is not integrable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The ratio of two independent normal variables, the denominator with positive variance and the numerator not almost surely zero (`(mN, vN) ≠ (0, 0)`), is not integrable.

results.title: Compliance types of Angrist, Imbens and Rubin
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: The four compliance types of Angrist, Imbens & Rubin (1996), determined by the pair of potential treatments `(D(0), D(1))`.

results.title: Compliance type of a pair of potential treatments
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The compliance type of the potential treatments `(D(0), D(1)) = (d₀, d₁)`.

results.title: Potential-outcomes model with binary instrument and treatment
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A potential-outcomes model with a binary instrument and a binary treatment (Imbens & Angrist 1994; Angrist, Imbens & Rubin 1996): the assigned instrument `Z`, the potential treatments `D(z)` and the potential outcomes `Y(z, d)`, all measurable. The observed treatment is `D(Z)` and the observed outcome `Y(Z, D(Z))`. The identifying assumptions (independence, exclusion, monotonicity, relevance) are separate predicates.

results.title: Observed treatment in a potential-outcomes model
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The observed treatment `D = D(Z)`.

results.title: Observed outcome in a potential-outcomes model
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The observed outcome `Y = Y(Z, D(Z))`.

results.title: Compliance type of a unit
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The compliance type of a unit.

results.title: Compliers in a potential-outcomes model
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The compliers, `D(0) = 0` and `D(1) = 1`.

results.title: Independence assumption for an instrument
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Independence (random assignment): the instrument is independent of the vector of all potential treatments and potential outcomes.

results.title: Exclusion restriction for an instrument
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Exclusion: the instrument affects the outcome only through the treatment, `Y(0, d) = Y(1, d)`.

results.title: Monotonicity assumption (no defiers)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Monotonicity: assignment never decreases the treatment, `D(0) ≤ D(1)`; there are no defiers.

results.title: Mean of a variable within an instrument arm
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The mean of `f` in the arm `Z = z`, `𝔼[f | Z = z]`, the expectation under the conditional measure. It is the junk value `0` when `P(Z = z) = 0`.

results.title: Observed treatment as a 0-1 real variable
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The observed treatment as a `0`/`1` real variable.

results.title: Wald instrumental-variable estimand
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Wald (instrumental-variable) estimand `(𝔼[Y | Z = 1] - 𝔼[Y | Z = 0]) / (𝔼[D | Z = 1] - 𝔼[D | Z = 0])`.

results.title: First stage: treatment-rate difference equals complier share
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The first stage (Imbens & Angrist 1994): under independence and monotonicity, with both arms of positive probability, the difference in treatment rates between the arms is the proportion of compliers.

results.title: Reduced form: outcome difference is the complier-weighted effect
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The reduced form (Imbens & Angrist 1994): under independence, exclusion and monotonicity, with integrable potential outcomes and both arms of positive probability, the difference in mean outcomes between the arms is `𝔼[(Y(z, 1) - Y(z, 0)) 1_complier]`, for either `z`.

results.title: Unrestricted algebraic identity behind the LATE theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The unrestricted algebraic identity behind LATE. If the complier set has measure zero, both sides totalize to `0`; therefore this theorem is not an identification or complier-average claim at that boundary. Use `waldEstimand_eq_late` for the source-faithful result with relevance.

results.title: Local average treatment effect theorem
